content.text:
**Finding submitted: COMPLIANT (preferred position) — no redline.**

**What I reviewed:** § 20 (Indemnification, p0083–p0087) in full, plus every cross-reference that could dilute it — § 21 Limitation of Liability and the "Excluded Claims" definition (§ 21.3), § 19.4–19.5 (warranty remedies and disclaimers), § 13–15 (licence, IP ownership, data/privacy), and full-document searches for "indemn", "hold harmless", "Customer shall defend", "infring" and "sole and exclusive remedy" to rule out a competing or broader Customer-side indemnity. None exists outside § 20.3.

**Why it clears preferred, element by element:**
- § 20.1 — express duty to **defend**, indemnify and hold harmless **Customer and its Affiliates** (plus directors/officers/employees/agents) against third-party claims that the **Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate** IP.
- § 20.2 — same protection for Vendor's **breach of Applicable Law**, **unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor**, and Vendor's **gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud** (also bodily injury/property damage).
- § 20.4 — full procedure: **prompt notice**, **reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense**, **control of the defence**, with delay excusing obligations only to the extent of material prejudice and a consent gate on settlements that admit fault or fail to release us.
- § 20.3 — Customer's indemnity is correctly **narrow**: unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, plus our own violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs where the claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions.

**Two points that run better than the fallback**, so no upgrade attempted:
- § 20.5 gives procure / modify-or-replace / terminate-and-refund remedies **"in addition to its defence obligations"** — not as a substitute cap on liability — and bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services.
- § 21.3 makes indemnification obligations, IP infringement and gross negligence/wilful misconduct **Excluded Claims**, so Vendor's indemnity is outside the § 21.1 cap altogether rather than limited to a 3× annual-fees super-cap.

**Noted in the rationale, not flagged:** § 20.1 contains no express Customer-modification / combination / specification exclusions. The fallback permits those exclusions rather than requiring them, and their absence broadens the indemnity in our favour — flagging it would argue against our own interest.
